[[File:Papaver hybridum MHNT.BOT.2021.17.33.jpg|thumb|''Papaver hybridum'']]

'''''Roemeria sicula''''', the '''rough poppy''' or '''round pricklyhead poppy''',<ref>{{Cite web|title=Papaver hybridum - Species Page - APA: Alabama Plant Atlas|url=http://floraofalabama.org/Plant.aspx?id=2814|access-date=2021-12-15|website=floraofalabama.org}}</ref> is a widespread species of flowering plant in the [[poppy family]]. It is native to the Mediterranean region, and western Asia as far as the western Himalayas, and has been introduced to much of the rest of Europe, South Africa, all of Australia, some US states, Chile and Argentina.<ref name="POWO 77319917-1" /><ref>{{cite web |title=''Papaver hybridum'' rough poppy |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/160227/Papaver-hybridum/Details |date=2021 |publisher=The Royal Horticultural Society |access-date=27 June 2021 }}</ref> It is a minor weed of cereal crops, and its range is expected to greatly expand due to climate change.<ref name = "1_of_1410_Google_Scholar_Hits" >{{cite journal |title=Assessment of weed establishment risk in a changing European climate |year=2012 |last1=Hyvönen |first1=Terho |last2=Luoto |first2=Miska |last3=Uotila |first3=Pertti |journal=Agricultural and Food Science |volume=21 |issue=4 |pages=348–360 |doi=10.23986/afsci.6321 |hdl=10138/165399 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
In 1753 [[Carl Linnaeus]] named a species ''Papaver hybridum'', but though not identical to ''Roemeria sicula'', it is regarded as one of its [[Synonym (botany)|synonyms]]. The first description identical to the present species was published by the botanist [[Giovanni Gussone]] in 1844 with the name ''Papaver siculum''. However, it was regarded as a [[subspecies]] or [[Variety (botany)|variety]] of ''Papaver hybridum'' by some botanists as late as 2007. More recently it has been moved to the genus ''[[Roemeria]]'' by Gabriele Galasso, Enrico Augusto Banfi, Llorenç Sáez, and Fabrizio Bartolucci.<ref name="POWO 77319917-1">{{cite POWO |id=77319917-1 |title=''Roemeria sicula'' (Guss.) Galasso, Banfi, L.Sáez & Bartolucci |access-date=20 December 2025}}</ref> Though ''Roemeria sicula'' is listed as the [[accepted name]] in [[Plants of the World Online]] and World Plants,<ref name="POWO 77319917-1" /><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Hassler |first1=Michael |date=11 November 2025 |title=''Roemeria sicula'' in Synonymic Checklist and Distribution of the World Flora. Version 25.11 |url= http://www.worldplants.de?name=Roemeria-sicula |website=World Plants |language=en |access-date=20 December 2025}}</ref> it is very frequently listed as ''Papaver hybridum'' by sources such as the USDA [[Natural Resources Conservation Service]],<ref>{{Cite usda plants|symbol=PAHY3 |title=Papaver hybridum |date=20 December 2025}}</ref> the [[Flora of North America]],<ref>{{Cite web <!--Deny Citation Bot-->|last1=FNA |date=5 November 2020 |orig-date=In print 1997 |url=https://floranorthamerica.org/Papaver_hybridum |title=''Papaver hybridum'' |website=[[Flora of North America]] |language=en |isbn=978-0-19-511246-7 |oclc=48601434 |access-date=20 December 2025}}</ref> and the Flora of Australia.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Kiger |first1=R.W. |date=19 February 2020 |title=''Papaver hybridum'' |url=https://profiles.ala.org.au/opus/foa/profile/Papaver%20hybridum |website=Flora of Australia |language=en-au |location=Canberra, Australia |publisher=Australian Biological Resources Study, Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water |access-date=20 December 2025}}</ref>
